appraisal_events.evidence: Stationed at the top of the great staircase, Charlus makes every guest come to greet him by name, in a performance the narrator explicitly calls prideful, while also comparing him half-admiringly, half-mockingly to a Wagnerian Margrave presiding over the Warburg.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus's staged, name-calling greeting visibly establishes his preeminent place at the reception, an elevation the narrator both grants and gently ironizes as vanity dressed in aesthetic grandeur.

appraisal_events.evidence: Mme d'Arpajon's already weak social power was further weakened by her liaison with the duc de Guermantes, and his abandonment of her delivered the final blow; meanwhile many eyes turn instead to the magnificent duchesse de Surgis-le-Duc, who has just succeeded her in Basin's heart.
appraisal_events.explanation: The duc de Guermantes's withdrawn favor is shown finishing off Mme d'Arpajon's standing, while the same shift in his affections visibly elevates duchesse de Surgis-le-Duc, who draws the room's attention on the balcony.

status_effects.explanation: Every guest is compelled to come pay him respects by name, a preeminence in the gathering that is witnessed and enacted before the whole party, even if the narrator frames it with some irony.

Her social power, already weak, is explicitly said to have been dealt a final blow by the duc de Guermantes's abandonment, a decline registered in the narration and visible in the crowd's attention turning elsewhere.
As the woman who has just succeeded Mme d'Arpajon in the duc de Guermantes's favor, she visibly draws the gaze of many guests toward her on the balcony, a witnessed rise in standing.
